somestacks.command.help.title: Some Stacks commands
somestacks.command.help.gate.operator: an operator, in game or from the server console
somestacks.command.help.gate.server_admi: a player meeting the configured gallery permission, in game only; galleries must be enabled
somestacks.command.help.unknown: No such ss command: %s. Try one of: %s
somestacks.command.help.deny.detail.1: A disabled mod's items are refused by every stack; a disabled item is refused on the deposit gestures. Contents already stored can still be taken out.
somestacks.command.help.deny.detail.2: Mod ids are lowercased and checked for valid namespace syntax; the mod need not be installed. Each mod list allows %s entries of at most %s characters.
somestacks.command.help.deny.summary: Bar a mod's items or one item from being stored
somestacks.command.help.gallery.detail.1: Builds east of you over a sandstone floor, nine items to a stack, rows running north. Whatever blocks stand in the floor and stack positions are replaced.
somestacks.command.help.gallery.detail.2: It overwrites that region outright, without the protection checks a placement gesture answers to.
somestacks.command.help.gallery.detail.3: <modid> is one namespace and all is every loaded one. list builds the namespaces of the gen mod list.
somestacks.command.help.gallery.detail.4: items builds one row from the gen item list, sorted by mod id and then item name.
somestacks.command.help.gallery.detail.5: all, list and items skip an entry they cannot show and report it; naming one namespace that cannot be shown fails instead.
somestacks.command.help.gallery.summary: Build galleries of Storage Stacks to review item rendering
somestacks.command.help.gen.detail.1: The mod list feeds /ss gallery list, /ss ingotgallery list, and /ss write list. Galleries build its namespaces in alphabetical order, one column each, and /ss gen mod list shows it in that order.
somestacks.command.help.gen.detail.2: The item list feeds /ss gallery items. The row is sorted by mod id and then item name when it is built.
somestacks.command.help.gen.detail.3: An item id is checked against the registry as it is added. Mod ids are lowercased and checked for valid namespace syntax. Each mod list allows %s entries of at most %s characters.
somestacks.command.help.gen.summary: Edit the mod and item lists the render galleries build from
somestacks.command.help.help.detail.1: Every ss subcommand has an entry. Render authoring and help are available to anyone; policy and list edits require an operator. Gallery access is controlled by server config because galleries overwrite the world.
somestacks.command.help.help.summary: List these commands, or explain one
somestacks.command.help.ingotgallery.det: The same generator as gallery but over Bar Stacks, covering only the items a Bar Stack accepts, one bar per ingot and eight to a block.
Its namespace completions offer only the namespaces that have an ingot.
somestacks.command.help.ingotgallery.sum: Build galleries of Bar Stacks to review bar textures and tints
somestacks.command.help.item.detail.1: Modes: 2d flattens the item onto the faces of its cell, 3d uses its ordinary model, block draws a block item's own block, and gui uses its inventory look.
somestacks.command.help.item.detail.2: Only the mode is required. Scale defaults to %s and offset to zero, and 2d uses the x and y offset only.
somestacks.command.help.item.detail.3: The change applies to your own view at once but lives in memory until /ss write changed saves it.
somestacks.command.help.item.detail.4: reset drops your entry, so the item goes back to the resource-pack or measured setting it had before.
somestacks.command.help.item.summary: Set how one item is drawn inside a stack
somestacks.command.help.reload.detail.1: Refreshes server policy and sends changed client-facing settings to every player. Fabric rereads the active TOML file; Forge loads TOML edits through its config lifecycle. Data-pack ingot tags use /reload; render resources use a resource reload.
somestacks.command.help.reload.summary: Re-read server policy, then re-sync players
somestacks.command.help.write.detail.1: changed saves what /ss item set to config/somestacks/item_overrides.json, which your client loads at startup. Only entries you set are ever written, and entries the file holds that cannot be used are kept as they are. A file that cannot be read is never overwritten.
somestacks.command.help.write.detail.2: The namespace forms dump a complete profile for every item of those namespaces to config/somestacks/generated_overrides/<namespace>.json, measuring whatever no override layer configures.
somestacks.command.help.write.detail.3: That dump runs on your own client and holds it busy until it finishes, so name a namespace, or keep a review session's mods in the gen mod list and dump list, rather than reaching for all in a large pack.
somestacks.command.help.write.detail.4: Nothing reads generated_overrides back. A file there is ready to be corrected by hand and dropped into a resource pack, including a server resource pack.
somestacks.command.help.write.summary: Write render overrides from your client to disk
